title: How to Care for a Georgette Anarkali: Washing, Storing and Steaming
excerpt: How to care for a georgette Anarkali at home: gentle washing, safe steaming, smart storage and gota lace care so your festive outfit lasts for years.
body:
To care for a georgette Anarkali, wash it rarely and gently, never wring it, steam instead of ironing, and store it folded in breathable cotton, away from damp and sunlight. Gota and handwork need extra attention: keep them dry, avoid rubbing and never fold sharply across the lace. Follow these simple habits and your Anarkali will look new for many festive seasons.

## Understand your fabric first

Georgette is a light, slightly crinkled fabric with a lovely fall, which is exactly why it is used for flared Anarkalis. Most georgette today is synthetic, which makes it fairly durable, but its open weave can snag, and its flowing panels can stretch out of shape if handled roughly. Gota lace is a woven metallic ribbon, and handwork may include threads, sequins or beads. These details are what make the outfit special, and they are also what need protecting.

Always check the care label or ask the seller before washing. When in doubt, choose the gentlest method.

## Washing: less is more

A festive Anarkali usually does not need washing after every wear. Air it out for a few hours after the party, spot clean small marks, and wash only when it really needs it.

| Situation | What to do |
|---|---|
| Worn once, no stains | Air it on a padded hanger, then store |
| Small food or makeup mark | Dab with cold water and a drop of mild detergent, then blot dry |
| Heavy embroidery or lots of gota | Professional dry clean is safest |
| Light handwork, full wash needed | Gentle hand wash in cold water |
| Sweat or perfume build-up | Hand wash, or dry clean if heavily embellished |

**How to hand wash:**

- Turn the Anarkali inside out to protect the gota and embroidery.
- Fill a tub with cold water and a small amount of mild liquid detergent.
- Soak for no more than ten minutes and swish gently. Do not scrub.
- Rinse in clean cold water until the soap is gone.
- Press out the water by rolling it in a thick towel. Never wring or twist.
- Dry flat or on a wide hanger in the shade. Direct sun can fade deep colours.

Wash the dupatta separately, especially if it has a different fabric or lace.

## Steaming instead of ironing

Georgette and metallic lace both dislike high direct heat. A handheld garment steamer is the best tool for a flared Anarkali, because it relaxes creases in the panels without flattening the fabric.

- Hang the outfit and hold the steamer a few centimetres away, moving down the panels.
- Steam the inside of the embroidered areas, not the front.
- If you must iron, use a low setting, turn the garment inside out and place a thin cotton cloth between the iron and the fabric.
- Never press directly on gota, sequins or beads.

A quick steam before an event also brings back the volume in the flare.

## Caring for gota and handwork

Gota is beautiful, but it can tarnish with moisture and lose its shine with friction. A few habits help:

- Keep perfume and deodorant away from the lace. Spray them before you dress and let them dry.
- After wearing, check for loose threads or lifting edges. A small stitch now prevents bigger damage later.
- Do not scrub embroidered areas, even when spot cleaning.
- Store with a layer of soft cotton or tissue over the gota so it does not rub on other fabric.

## Storing your Anarkali

Long, flared outfits stretch if hung for months, because the weight of the panels pulls on the shoulders. For long storage, fold instead.

- Fold the Anarkali loosely along the panels, with tissue paper between the folds.
- Avoid folding sharply across embroidery or lace.
- Wrap it in a cotton saree cover or an old cotton dupatta. Plastic traps moisture.
- Add a sachet of dried neem leaves or cloves to deter insects. Avoid placing mothballs directly against the fabric.
- Refold in a different way every few months so permanent creases do not form.

For short-term storage between events, a padded hanger works well.

## Travelling with it

Many women abroad carry their festive outfits to weddings and Diwali gatherings. Roll the Anarkali loosely in tissue and cotton, pack it on top of your suitcase, and hang it in the bathroom while you shower on arrival so the steam relaxes the creases. ## Frequently asked questions

**Can I machine wash a georgette Anarkali?**
It is not recommended for embellished pieces. A plain georgette Anarkali may survive a delicate cycle in a mesh bag, but hand washing or dry cleaning is far safer for gota and handwork.

**How do I remove creases from georgette?**
Use a garment steamer, or hang the outfit in a steamy bathroom. If ironing, keep it on low heat with a cloth in between.

**Why has my gota turned dull?**
Moisture, perfume and friction can dull metallic lace. Keep it dry, store it wrapped in cotton and avoid spraying fragrance near it.

**Should I hang or fold my Anarkali?**
Hang it for a few days between events, but fold it for long storage so the weight of the flare does not stretch the shoulders.
